implementation: Pass the already-computed marker-like morphology plane into line-intersection analysis. Leave a candidate reviewable if any pixel in its existing five-by-five mask footprint reaches the existing 0.5 mask boundary.
Preserve all line geometry, model weights, crop rules, classification thresholds and suppression distances. Advance the residual composition/cache identity to raster-residual-v4-marker-core-review.

Eight new cases cover filled cores of two sizes with offset centers and connecting strokes. Existing two-line crossings remain masked. A dense three-line crossing also remains reviewable because the existing morphology descriptor identifies conflicting marker-like ink.
integration_decision: Retain the conservative conflict guard so line geometry alone cannot suppress ink carrying contrary marker-like evidence. The native accuracy tradeoff is not an improvement: one truth is recovered and two are lost per arm, with one additional false detection. Keep these losses open and continue marker diagnosis. Shared gates and production approval remain failed.

limitations: Native recall falls from 741 to 740 of 838 in V44 and 745 to 744 in V46. Extras rise from 27 to 28 and 21 to 22. A recovered filled square does not offset two lost truths in the crowded hexagonal-marker scene.
The structural descriptor can also mark a dense three-line crossing as marker-like. Such conflicts now remain reviewable; this does not prove a true marker is present.
The mask shadow removed masks near thirteen currently missed native truths per arm. Only one truth was actually recovered in each complete workflow. Mask removal is not a recovery metric.
